Architecture

How the
system works

A cloud-to-edge architecture: your PMS syncs to Google Cloud, which pushes updates every 60 seconds to Raspberry Pi units running Home Assistant on-property.

01

PMS triggers event

Check-in, checkout or key changes fire a webhook to the Livinis cloud API on Google App Engine.

02

Cloud processes & persists

The API updates Cloud SQL and writes per-property JSON files to a shared Google Drive folder.

03

Local sync via rclone

Each Raspberry Pi polls Drive every 60 seconds, keeping door codes and room states local and current.

04

Home Assistant acts

Node-RED automations read local files and control locks, thermostats and lighting — even offline.

A day in the life

How a stay works
with Livinis

From the moment a guest checks in to the moment they leave, every step is automated. No manual resets. No forgotten keys. No wasted energy.

Step 01
Check-in

PMS check-in triggers automatic keycard creation

The moment a guest checks in via your PMS, Livinis creates and activates keycards for their room, connected rooms and common areas. Cards are time-limited to the booking period. No front desk action required.

Step 02
Room entry

Smart pocket activates room on valid card only

The active key pocket reads the card UID and profile. Only a valid, associated card enables power, lighting and climate. A welcome lighting scene activates. Room status updates to "occupied" on the reception dashboard.

Step 03
During stay

Climate, energy and housekeeping fully automated

Guest sets their preferred temperature — the system remembers it. If the window opens, HVAC pauses automatically. Housekeeping is blocked from entering while the guest card is in the pocket. DND enforced without a sign on the door.

Step 04
Checkout

All keycards deactivated, room reset to standby

Checkout via PMS (or optional drop-box) instantly deactivates all keycards for the booking. Temperature resets to the standard profile. Housekeeping is notified. The room is ready for the next guest within minutes.

Key feature

The active
key pocket

Traditional key pockets activate power with any card — even an expired or invalid one. Livinis active pockets read the card UID and profile, enabling power only when the card is valid and associated with that room.

No wasted energy — room powers down when guest leaves
No unauthorised access — expired cards rejected at the pocket
Instant status update — reception sees occupied/vacant in real time
Traditional pocket
Any card = power on

No validation. Expired, stolen or random cards activate the room. Energy wasted, security compromised.

Livinis active pocket
Valid card = power on

Reads UID and booking profile. Only activates on valid, associated cards. Full audit trail.

Yes. The Raspberry Pi edge units cache all access data locally and continue controlling doors, thermostats and lighting even when the cloud connection is temporarily unavailable. Data syncs automatically when connectivity is restored.

Livinis integrates with Clock PMS in production. Any PMS that supports webhooks or API events (check-in, checkout, room changes) can be integrated. We handle the implementation — your team just uses your existing PMS as usual.

It depends on the property size and existing infrastructure. A typical boutique hotel (20–50 rooms) can be fully operational in 2–4 weeks including hardware installation, software configuration and staff training.

From the Concierge dashboard, staff can instantly deactivate all cards linked to a booking and issue new ones. No locksmith, no hardware change. The new cards are active within 60 seconds. The lost card becomes permanently invalid.

Yes. A single card can be configured to open multiple rooms and areas — ideal for families (parents accessing children's rooms), connected rooms, or guests who need access to ancillary facilities such as the garage, gym or sauna.

Within approximately 60 seconds. The PMS webhook triggers the cloud API, which updates the access database and pushes new JSON files to Google Drive. The on-site Raspberry Pi syncs every 60 seconds and activates the card immediately.

Google Analytics

We use Google Analytics (GA4) to understand how visitors interact with our website. Google Analytics collects information anonymously and reports website trends without identifying individual visitors. IP addresses are anonymised. Your choices

You can choose to accept or reject non-essential cookies at any time. Rejecting analytics cookies will disable Google Analytics tracking. Note that essential cookies (such as your consent preference) cannot be disabled as they are required for the website to function.

You can also delete cookies already stored on your computer through your browser settings. Please note that deleting or blocking cookies may impact your user experience.
